bluf: Ukraine has stabilized the frontline and regained territory following Russia's loss of Starlink, while Ukraine's deep strikes into Russian defense industrial and energy infrastructure are imposing cumulative costs. Russia's large-scale nuclear exercises with Belarus and failure to secure the Power of Siberia-2 pipeline from China highlight strategic constraints, even as the Kremlin remains committed to maximalist war aims. Concurrently, Iran's coercion of Strait of Hormuz shipping is prompting NATO to consider an escort mission by July, directly threatening European energy security and requiring contingency planning.

sections.title: Ukraine Frontline Dynamics and Counterstrike Campaign
sections.content: Ukraine's defenses are stabilizing the frontline, with the US Defense Intelligence Agency and NATO Secretary General noting territorial gains following Russian forces' loss of Starlink access in early February 2026 (Article 1). Ukraine's Fortress Belt—a concentration of four large cities—remains the cornerstone of a defensible frontline, and the Kremlin seeks a political settlement to gain this critical terrain without a fight (Article 4). Ukrainian forces conducted a large-scale strike on Moscow City and Oblast on May 16-17, hitting the Angstrem Semiconductor Plant, the Moscow Oil Refinery, and multiple oil pumping stations, degrading Russian military-industrial capacity (Article 15). Russia responded with a massive strike of 546 drones and missiles on May 17-18, heavily targeting Dnipro and civilian infrastructure, including a Chinese-owned ship in Odesa (Article 13). Ukraine's new domestically produced glide bomb will expand its air interdiction capabilities (Article 13).
sources: Ukraine’s Fortress Belt: The Key to Sustaining the Frontline

sections.title: Russia's Strategic Posture and Geopolitical Constraints
sections.content: Russia and Belarus completed combined nuclear exercises on May 21, deploying nuclear munitions to Belarus and launching ICBMs, hypersonic missiles, and cruise missiles—signaling deepened de facto control over Belarus (Article 5). The unannounced exercise, involving over 64,000 personnel, is meant to posture strength and distract from mounting battlefield weaknesses (Article 10). Meanwhile, President Putin failed to secure a deal on the Power of Siberia-2 pipeline during his visit to China, signing only minor bilateral agreements—underscoring the limits of Sino-Russian cooperation as China extracts concessions (Article 8). Bloomberg reports that senior Kremlin officials view the war as a 'dead end,' but Putin remains committed to seizing all of Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts by end of 2026 (Article 1). Russia's occupation efforts in Ukraine continue with child deportations and cultural integration programs funded by state-backed initiatives (Article 7).

sections.title: Iran's Strait of Hormuz Coercion and NATO Response
sections.content: Iran is using the ceasefire to normalize its control over Strait of Hormuz transit, demanding vessels obtain Iranian 'permission' and pay fees—a protection racket that frames Iranian naval presence as a security service (Articles 2, 9). Iran's latest counterproposal does not meet US demands, and uranium enrichment and Strait control remain sticking points; a planned US strike was canceled at Qatari, Emirati, and Saudi leaders' request (Article 14). Some NATO countries support a plan to escort ships through the strait beginning in early July if Iran continues its blockade, though unanimous backing is lacking (Article 11). The attack on the South Korean-operated vessel Namu-ho, attributed to Iran, is prompting South Korea to consider joining the US-led Maritime Freedom Construct coalition—potentially involving European allies (Article 12). Iran also analyzed US aircraft flight patterns, indicating efforts to improve targeting of allied aircraft (Article 11).

key_developments: Ukraine regains territory after Russia loses Starlink access; DIA and NATO confirm frontline stabilization.
Russia conducts surprise large-scale nuclear exercise with Belarus, deploying nuclear weapons on Belarusian soil.
Putin fails to secure Power of Siberia-2 pipeline deal with China, highlighting limits of bilateral cooperation.
Ukraine strikes deep into Moscow area, hitting a semiconductor plant, oil refinery, and pumping stations.
NATO considers escort mission in Strait of Hormuz starting July due to Iran's protection racket and attacks on shipping.
Iran's latest counterproposal to US does not address uranium enrichment or Strait controls; US cancels planned strike at Gulf states' urging.
outlook: Ukraine will likely sustain its deep strike campaign and consolidate territorial gains, while Russia escalates nuclear signaling and continues grinding offensive operations. The Strait of Hormuz crisis will push NATO toward a naval deployment by mid-summer, increasing the risk of direct confrontation with Iran and exacerbating energy price volatility for Europe.
